# Bug Catalog: `verify/spell_playtest.gd`

**Generated by /design-tests on 2026-10-01**  
**Scope:** the `?spell_playtest=1` title route, `World._on_title_spell_playtest()`,
the SpellTree data contract, and Party Spells visibility.

## What this test covers

The Spell Test title route is a fast, non-saving human-review entry point. It
must leave reviewers with actual learned and equipped spells they can inspect
in the Party Spells menu. It is not a substitute for the normal post-victory
automatic-unlock flow.

## Public interface

| Symbol | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `?spell_playtest=1` / `--spell-playtest` | review route | exposes the Spell Test title action |
| `World._on_title_spell_playtest()` | title-action handler | prepares the temporary review state |
| `World._inventory_spells_for()` | player-menu data source | returns spells visible in Party Spells |
| `SpellTree.learn_all_available()` | progression rule | learns/equips all spells available from supplied points and keys |

## IO boundaries

- Browser query string / command line selects the route.
- The normal game writes save slots; this review route deliberately uses no
  active slot and must not write one.
- No network or time dependency is involved in the behavior tested here.

## Bug catalog

| # | Bug | Blast radius | Plausibility | Test type | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The Spell Test grants points and keys but leaves every spell unlearned, so Party Spells says there are none. | High: the advertised human-review route cannot review spells. | This was observed manually; the old test directly called `SpellTree.learn()` after the route. | captured-bug contract | open |
| 2 | A route learns spells but fails to equip them or expose any inventory-tagged spell in Party Spells. | Medium: review can see data but cannot validate usable spell presentation. | Known and equipped lists are separate persisted fields; only some spells are inventory-usable. | invariant | open |
| 3 | The test route accidentally writes progress into a player save slot. | Medium: review links can corrupt a reviewer’s real run. | Title handlers explicitly manage `_current_slot`; this route intentionally uses `-1`. | negative-path | open |

## Test plan

### Bug #1 — empty spell-review route

- **Test type:** captured-bug contract
- **Description string:**
  > `spell playtest: title route provides learned spells — guards against empty Party Spells`
- **What it catches:** the real regression where the route supplied resources
  but did not invoke normal learning, leaving all `known_spells` empty.
- **Self-critique:**
  - Could this pass for wrong-but-stable output? No. A route that displays no
    learned spell fails the observable roster assertion.
  - Could this fail under a behavior-preserving refactor? No. It does not
    assert a particular UI node or helper implementation.

### Bug #2 — learned but not usable

- **Test type:** invariant
- **Description string:**
  > `spell playtest: learned spells are equipped and Party Spells has support actions — guards against dead review content`
- **What it catches:** disconnects between learning, battle equipment, and the
  pause-menu data source.
- **Self-critique:**
  - Could this pass for wrong-but-stable output? No. It requires every learned
    spell to be equipped and at least one actual Party Spells action.
  - Could this fail under a behavior-preserving refactor? No. It observes
    durable roster state and the player-menu data source, not scene internals.

### Bug #3 — review route writes a save

- **Test type:** negative-path
- **Description string:**
  > `spell playtest: review route remains unsaved — guards against test-link save corruption`
- **What it catches:** assigning the route a normal slot by accident.
- **Self-critique:**
  - Could this pass for wrong-but-stable output? No. An active save slot is the
    harmful state regardless of implementation.
  - Could this fail under a behavior-preserving refactor? No.

## Skipped

- Manual browser layout, tooltip readability, and successful in-combat spell
  casts — visual/end-to-end concerns; they require the hosted playtest and are
  not honestly covered by this headless contract.
- Normal post-victory automatic unlock — a separate progression test should
  cover a real non-tutorial victory; this route intentionally starts with a
  prepared roster.
- Exact number/order of visible spell buttons — cosmetic/data-content detail,
  not the route contract.

## Post-write evaluation

- **Bugs caught** (test failed against current code, fix required): #1 and
  #2. The original title action granted 99 points and keys but learned no
  spells; every `known_spells`/`equipped_spells` assertion and the Party
  Spells invariant failed.
- **Bugs characterized** (test passes; behavior pinned): #3. The repaired
  route keeps `_current_slot == -1`, so it remains non-saving review plumbing.
- **Bugs discovered during writing** not in the original catalog: the old
  verification directly called `SpellTree.learn()` after entering the route,
  which made a non-functional player flow look green.
- **Tests removed** (failed self-critique mid-write): the obsolete assertion
  that each diver still has 99 points. A correct route spends those supplied
  points while learning spells, so the durable behavior is learned/equipped
  coverage, not an unchanged resource count.
